newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission to press ahead with olive oil proposal.
newsitem.headline: Commission to press ahead with olive oil proposal.

text.p: BRUSSELS, Oct 16 (REUTER) - The European Commission is likely to reject demands for further changes to its plans to reform the olive oil regime, an EU official said on Wednesday.
"Officials in the Commission are making it clear that they have no intention of giving way. They expect a proposal to be published in about two weeks time," the official said.
Officials say that any delay in producing a proposal would risk allowing producers to step up production.

"Commission officials say that there should be no need for further discussion which would delay the proposal for up to a year," the official said, noting the reform was scheduled as part of the 1992 reform of the Common Agriculture Policy (CAP).

COPA and COGECA, the European farmers and farm cooperative organisations which organised a protest in Brussels last week, say that Commissioner Franz Fischler's proposals will lead to a reduction in quality and a fall in incomes.
The two organisations favour granting producer aid on the basis of quality and the continuation of the current intervention price support system.
The Commission has often said that the highest levels of agricultural fraud are in the olive oil sector.
A Commission official said, "It is too early to judge what will be in the proposal. It is not yet complete."
